clauses.text: At Intermarché in Gradignan, reporting describes a cold room reaching 50°C, a sprinkler activating and reserve-area flooding. relations.rationale: The prolonged defrost and resulting conditions show why the command scope matters. The initiating account, authority over the original task and subsequent target or action change are unknown. An intrusion alone does not demonstrate that an existing maintenance permission was treated as authority for these changes.

clauses.text: Haguenau Intermarché reported cabinet readings of 32°C, approximately €50,000 in frozen-stock losses and an additional smaller chilled-stock loss. This is one retailer’s consequence account, not a national loss estimate or evidence of a particular authentication or control mechanism.

The separate E.Leclerc store in Haguenau described settings up to 50°C and discarded frozen goods. It is a different affected retailer from the nearby Intermarché. The report does not establish that the same command, credential or response route operated at both.

Super U Mirepoix managers described a remote-monitoring warning at 2 am, staff attendance and a refrigeration technician arriving at 6 am. They reported approximately €90,000 in losses from the affected display areas; reserves and cold rooms remained unaffected. Warning delivery, repair attendance and the surviving stock are distinct observations. The source does not define a guaranteed protection threshold or establish why reserves escaped the interference.

relations.rationale: The reported monitoring warning reached people who responded, while some stock was still lost and reserves were unaffected. The missing facts are the control’s required protective purpose, applicable response time and the causal link between the response and the spared reserves. The outcome therefore establishes neither inadequate effect under this class nor a separately verified invariant-held result.

clauses.text: Coopérative U’s president reported 80 affected stores and said most avoided a cold-chain break or stock destruction through the response of teams and refrigeration specialists. He also said a minority could not react or control the interference quickly enough. This does not establish that 80 stores lost stock, or that the same protective mechanism operated at every store.

relations.rationale: The retailer’s account supports distinct protected and harmed outcomes. It does not identify the particular activated controls, their required protective levels or store-specific intervention traces. Those missing links prevent attributing the avoided losses to a validated control effect under this class; the observed response remains part of the occurrence.

clauses.text: Intermarché La Haye-du-Puits reported approximately US$112,000 in discarded food and heat-affected equipment. These are attributed consequences at one store. The reported losses and hardware damage do not identify the remote command source, a participating AI system or a uniform national mechanism.

Censys observed 1,825 Internet-exposed Danfoss StoreView hosts in France on 11 October and 537 on 14 October. These are two exposure measurements, not a count of compromised stores. A reduction in visible hosts does not by itself establish restoration, valid access control or attribution of the earlier commands.

AIOpsShield sanitised attacker-controlled telemetry before agent ingestion. In the reported rerun, the injected repairs did not succeed. This establishes containment for the tested telemetry route, not protection against other poisoned inputs or compromised tools.

clauses.text: Researchers supplied one request-field payload containing a false SSL diagnosis and an nginx repair direction. The application copied both into its logs. These are two statements in the same injected passage, not two separate injections.

The GPT-4o Flash agent read the planted passage, adopted the false diagnosis and the proposed repair. The authors describe execution for this SocialNet example. Their aggregate metric measures matching remediation output, not execution in every run.

relations.rationale: The log entry contained the attacker’s explanation of why HTTP errors were occurring. The agent used that explanation as support for its root-cause conclusion, although the person supplying the request field was also causing the logged errors. Recording the text in an application log did not independently corroborate it. The trust problem is the adoption of that diagnosis; the repair instruction in the same payload requires its own authority assessment.

The payload did more than describe an error: it directed the agent to add a package source and upgrade nginx. The requester could supply application input but had no established authority to instruct the incident-response agent. The agent nevertheless adopted that repair after retrieving the log. The direction’s apparent relevance to the fault did not make it an authorised operational instruction. The authors describe execution in this example; their aggregate output-matching score does not prove execution in every trial.

clauses.text: The researchers evaluated agent/model/application combinations and reported output matching. This is evidence of adversarial evaluation; discovering a susceptible configuration does not show that the researchers omitted testing.

sources.title: FalseCrashReducer: Mitigating False Positive Crashes in OSS-Fuzz-Gen Using Agentic AI

access.access_method: Read the public source text. No attack code or fuzzing experiment was executed.
limitations: First-party study. Prose and Table 2 totals differ. Neither independent reproduction nor raw-data reconciliation was performed.

mappings.basis: AI-generated drivers called internal functions outside valid calling conditions. The resulting crash artefacts were treated as program-error evidence even though later context validation identified additional driver errors. The crash was real in the constructed harness, but its interpretation as a reachable application defect lacked the assurance required for defect triage.

The added validator traced one crash through the application entry point and found an input-length check that made the crashing path infeasible in normal use. It rejected that candidate with source-code evidence. This bounded check does not validate every rejection.

clauses.text: Figures 1–2 show the libraw example. The generated driver passes a buffer of arbitrary bytes into a function that casts the pointer to a CrxImage structure and accesses its fields. A buffer that is too small can crash this test because the driver has not constructed the valid object expected by the function. Where normal callers enforce those conditions, the crash does not establish a defect reachable from the application’s entry point. Sections 5.2.3 and 5.3.2 separately report that contextual validation rejected additional crashes initially classified as program errors.

relations.rationale: The generated driver supplied arbitrary bytes where the target function expected a valid image object. A crash under that invalid calling condition establishes that the constructed test crashed, not that normal application use can trigger the same fault. The evaluated workflow still labelled some such outcomes as program errors until a later validator examined their calling context. Treating the crash as application-defect evidence before establishing that connection gave the test artefact more diagnostic assurance than it supported.

clauses.text: The added validator traced one crash through the application entry point and found an input-length check that made the crashing path infeasible in normal use. It rejected that candidate with source-code evidence. This bounded check does not validate every rejection.

relations.rationale: The added validator traced one crash through the application entry point and found an input-length check that made the crashing path infeasible in normal use. It rejected that candidate with source-code evidence. This bounded check does not validate every rejection.

clauses.text: Manual review found reliable conclusions in 10 of 20 added-validator analyses. Other analyses mislocated crashes or misjudged calling conditions. Repeated-run consistency was also incomplete. A rejection by this validator therefore does not independently establish ground truth.

relations.rationale: The added validator also produced unsupported feasibility conclusions in the manually reviewed sample. Those judgements cannot receive verified-defect or verified-rejection status merely because another agent produced them. The reported reliability review limits reliance on its aggregate filtering result.
